title: More than meets the eye: intensity of warming-induced risks in recently diversified Gymnocalycium species across Argentine montane ecosystems
content:
Abstract
Global cactus diversity faces significant threats under global warming conditions. In this study, we investigated the intraspecific genetic diversity of four Gymnocalycium species (G. andreae, G. baldianum, G. monvillei, and G. pugionacanthum) distributed in the Sierras Pampeanas of central Argentina and analysed their responses to climate change. We used chloroplast intergenic spacers (trnL-trnF and trnH-psbA) to assess intraspecific genetic variation. A Bayesian phylogenetic approach was employed to estimate haplotype divergence times. Ellipsoid-based niche models were implemented, and a niche overlap analysis was performed. We found overall low intraspecific genetic variation. Intraspecific diversification of all species occurred between 450 and 180 kya, coinciding with a period of intensified glacial cycles. Most species exhibited a north–south clustering of specific haplotypes. As temperatures warm, upslope migration was predicted for all species, accompanied by drastic range contractions that could possibly lead to the extinction of G. andreae. Among the phylogenetically related species pairs (G. andreae–G. baldianum and G. monvillei–G. pugionacanthum), considerable niche overlap was detected only in the latter pair. Pleistocene climatic fluctuations played a critical role in shaping intraspecific diversification. Ex situ conservation and population retranslocation are recommended, as ant-mediated seed dispersal is unlikely to transport seeds to higher elevations under warming conditions.
